principles: Fail closed on stale, missing, mismatched, unbound, or overclaiming evidence.
Keep Quantum M3 local and read-only; no lifecycle mutation or evidence writing.
Expose human-readable and JSON guidance that names repair/degrade/escalate/stop actions.
Preserve explicit no-theory, no-hardware, no-production, and no-Authority boundaries.
Do not consume M4 benchmark or M5 report/governance scope early.
drivers: M3 must build on the existing Quantum M0-M2 evaluator and adapter normalization without replacing them.
Hosts need an executable command surface, not only prose, to inspect quantum claim admissibility.
Reviewers must be able to verify behavior through deterministic local smoke and docs.

options.name: pure-helper-plus-readonly-command
pros: Keeps policy decisions deterministic and testable in core quantum helpers.
Gives hosts a concrete quantum_claim_check command without mutating lifecycle state.
Leaves M4 benchmark and M5 reporting as separate milestones.
cons: Does not automatically block Story transitions; hosts must consume the diagnostic output intentionally.
Requires command wiring and docs updates in addition to core helper code.

options.name: global-story-machine-integration
pros: Would make Quantum gate decisions first-class lifecycle blockers immediately.
Could reduce host discretion for quantum stories.
cons: Too broad for M3 and risks changing non-quantum Story transitions.
Harder to review safely and conflicts with the story scope exclusion for global lifecycle mutation.

options.name: docs-only-policy-description
cons: Fails the user request for executable Quantum capability.
Does not provide a reusable command or deterministic proof surface for M4/M5.

rationale: A pure helper plus read-only command gives Quantum M3 real executable capability while preserving Proof-or-Stop boundaries and leaving benchmark/reporting/global lifecycle mutation for later stories.

preMortem.scenario: M3 accidentally claims production or Authority readiness.
preMortem.trigger: Command output or docs use generic readiness wording without boundary booleans.
preMortem.consequence: Hosts may treat local quantum claim admissibility as external completion proof.
preMortem.mitigation: Expose authorityDone=false and productionDone=false in command output and smoke-test the boundary wording.

preMortem.trigger: Implementation adds A1-A4/B1-B15 aggregate metrics instead of a few named demo cases.
preMortem.consequence: Milestone boundaries blur and benchmark evidence becomes unreviewed.
preMortem.mitigation: Limit M3 smoke to complete/weak/overclaim demos and reserve rate metrics/confidence intervals for M4.

preMortem.trigger: Handler writes gate evidence or calls story transition helpers.
preMortem.consequence: Read-only diagnostic command becomes a hidden lifecycle actor.
preMortem.mitigation: Command policy marks quantum_claim_check readOnly, tests assert no production/Authority claims, and docs state no Story machine mutation.

preMortem.scenario: Docs overclaim generic framework milestone completion.
preMortem.trigger: Updating claim-admissibility-adapter-pack-framework.md says generic gate-policy adapter M4 is done because Quantum M3 is done.
preMortem.consequence: Future pack authors misunderstand framework status.
preMortem.mitigation: Document Quantum-specific M3 runtime status only and preserve generic framework future milestones.
